title: Bat Talk and Tour
location: Yolo Basin Foundation, Yolo Bypass Wildlife Area
description:
The Bats are Back at the Yolo Causeway 
  
Summer is here, and the bats are back!  
  
Join Yolo Basin Foundation this summer on a Bat Talk and Tour. Learn about these amazing flying mammals that do so much to help reduce insect pests throughout the area. Live native bat species are displayed as part of the presentation. The program culminates in watching the bats as they emerge from under the freeway. 
  
The maternity Mexican free-tailed bat colony under the I-80 Yolo Causeway is growing daily as they return from wherever they spent the winter. Although many of the bats over-winter in the bridge, most seem to leave. As the weather warms, crops grow and insect populations explode, the bats return to the Causeway.  
  
These amazing, winged wonders are mammals that fly. Each summer the females give birth, in late June, to one pup. She nurses that pup for about 5 to 6 weeks, and then it joins her as she flies throughout the Central Valley to consume crop pests and mosquitos. There also are males that live in the Yolo Causeway bridge. 
  
Throughout the summer, Yolo Basin Foundation offers many opportunities to learn more about the bats. Registration is now open.  
  
Children who are interested in bats are encouraged to join Yolo Basin Foundation for a morning of “Bats and Crafts”.  Meet live bats from our local area then have fun creating crafts and playing bat games. This special event is aimed at young children, especially those that are too young to stay up late to watch the bats fly. 
  
All events and some fun fact videos about our programs and the bats can be found at https://yolobasin.org/battalkandtour/ . 
  
Yolo Basin Foundation offers environmental education programs for all ages related to wetlands and wildlife.

title: Aiko Shimada Jazz Quintet Live @ The Melon Ball
location: Watermelon Music, 1970 Lake Blvd, DAVIS, CA, 95616, United States
description:
Watermelon Music in Davis presents Aiko Shimada Jazz Quintet. 
Aiko Shimada is a Sacramento-based jazz vocalist known for a warm, ethereal tone and an honest, restrained approach to interpretation. 
Once a singer-guitarist/songwriter who performed and toured widely for decades in Seattle, she now returns to jazz, blending beloved standards with originals and thoughtful covers. 
Notable collaborators include the late world-renowned pianist Jessica Williams, and acclaimed jazz guitarist Bill Frisell appears on her album Blue Marble (John Zorn’s Tzadik Label in New York). 
Joined by Selena Delgadillo (piano), Mark Collins (upright bass), Stephen Esquivido (sax), and Aidan Smith (drums), Aiko offers an evening of elegance, intimacy, and sincerity shaped by influences from Billie Holiday and Shirley Horn to Thelonious Monk, Miles Davis, Cassandra Wilson, Egberto Gismonti, and Brazilian singer Mônica Salmaso. 
Press 
“Stunning live” — The Stranger, Seattle
“Beautiful, profound, and original… haunting, mature, unforgettable.” — Steve Silberman, Wired
“Shimada is one of the most original and creative musicians on the Seattle scene.” — Seattle Times
“Her music is a fluid and exquisitely ear-friendly blend of lower Manhattan jazz and textural forms…” — Sacramento News & Review 
Instagram: @aikoshimada.music
YouTube: Aiko Shimada Music & Beyond 
This is a BOYB show!  Watermelon Music serves non-alcoholic drinks and pre-packaged snacks. 
$15 General Admission
$10 Students (available in-store or at the door only)
Kids under 12 are FREE!

title: Bat Talk and Tour
location: Yolo Basin Foundation, Yolo Bypass Wildlife Area
description:
The Bats are Back at the Yolo Causeway 
  
Summer is here, and the bats are back!  
  
Join Yolo Basin Foundation this summer on a Bat Talk and Tour. Learn about these amazing flying mammals that do so much to help reduce insect pests throughout the area. Live native bat species are displayed as part of the presentation. The program culminates in watching the bats as they emerge from under the freeway. 
  
The maternity Mexican free-tailed bat colony under the I-80 Yolo Causeway is growing daily as they return from wherever they spent the winter. Although many of the bats over-winter in the bridge, most seem to leave. As the weather warms, crops grow and insect populations explode, the bats return to the Causeway.  
  
These amazing, winged wonders are mammals that fly. Each summer the females give birth, in late June, to one pup. She nurses that pup for about 5 to 6 weeks, and then it joins her as she flies throughout the Central Valley to consume crop pests and mosquitos. There also are males that live in the Yolo Causeway bridge. 
  
Throughout the summer, Yolo Basin Foundation offers many opportunities to learn more about the bats. Registration is now open.  
  
Children who are interested in bats are encouraged to join Yolo Basin Foundation for a morning of “Bats and Crafts”.  Meet live bats from our local area then have fun creating crafts and playing bat games. This special event is aimed at young children, especially those that are too young to stay up late to watch the bats fly. 
  
All events and some fun fact videos about our programs and the bats can be found at https://yolobasin.org/battalkandtour/ . 
  
Yolo Basin Foundation offers environmental education programs for all ages related to wetlands and wildlife.

title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.
source: Meetup Yolo County Board Game Gathering

title: Davis Music Festival

description:
Davis Music Festival (DMF) is a three day multi-venue, multi-genre live music event showcasing local, regional and touring artists – all to benefit our local public schools’ art, music and performing arts programs… all proceeds are donated to to support local arts education and performance opportunities for up and coming artists. It’s like our own version of SXSW in a single weekend, and for a great cause! 
This event is all ages. The festival takes place rain or shine (though we probably will never have to worry about rain on a June day in Davis, CA). Tickets are non-refundable and non-transferable. Lineup and daily schedules are subject to change. Artist cancellation is not grounds for refund. 
For further information and questions, visit davismusicfest.com. If you are experiencing any technical issues related to online ticketing, please contact us at info@davismusicfest.com

title: Bat Talk & Walk Tour
location: Yolo Basin Foundation, Yolo Bypass Wildlife Area
description:
Bat Talk & Walk Tour is back in Davis! 
Following a presentation on bat natural history, where you will have the opportunity to see live ambassador bats up close, the group will carpool out to the Yolo Bypass Wildlife Area for a brief tour of the wetlands and rice fields. Then we get in position to watch the “flyout” of the largest urban colony of Mexican free-tailed bats in California. The bats emerge in long ribbons as they head out to hunt for insects for the night. 
  
The whole experience takes about two and a half hours. This is a family friendly event! There is a small amount of walking. Those in wheelchairs or unable to walk may view the bats by car. Please let us know if you have special needs. 
  
Refunding or rescheduling tickets requires two weeks notice and is subject to a $10 administrative fee. 
  
In regards to the recent heat: While it can be very hot in town during the heat of the day, the first hour and a half of this program will take place in an air conditioned room and from your own vehicle during the auto tour. By the time we are outside to view the flyout, it will be nearly sunset. It is typically 10-15 degrees cooler in the Yolo Bypass Wildlife Area where we watch the bat flyout. 
Tickets are $17 adult, $5 child (6-17 years old), children under 5 years old are free.

title: Park Winters Garden Tour
location: Park Winters, Park Winters, 27850 County Road 26 Winters, CA 95694
description:
Park Winters is surrounded by hundreds of acres of farmland with unobstructed views of the Berryessa Blue Ridge Reserve. Originally planted in 1865, our gardens take you back in time—now lovingly curated, manicured and maintained. 
Join us for a guided tour, take in the beauty of 150 year old trees and stroll through our sunken garden filled with lavender and snowy white roses. The classic cypress trees soar and native songbirds call as we experience the scents and scenes of the western Yolo County countryside. This experience is approximately a 90 minute walking tour, 
*Garden Tours are on the 2nd and 4th Saturday’s of each month, with exception for July – August, when we take a pause due to high temperatures – Garden Tours will resume in September.

description:
Weird Harold returns to the Melon Ball in Davis this summer for one night only! 
How does one describe Weird Harold?  They’ve engaged and befuddled local audiences since the 1990’s with their loud, raucous, hard-rockin’, quirky, hilarious, energetic, entertaining, indie alternative ear worms, such as “I Drive a Monster Truck,” “I Ruined Your Birthday,” “I’ve Got a Bad Rash,” and the Steinbeck “Of Mice and Men”-inspired “Be My Bunny.” Count on an evening of high-energy, seventh-grade style double entendre potty humor, and head-boppin,’ eye-poppin’ entertainment!  Weird Harold cannot be explained, only experienced, and no two shows are the same, even if they perform the same set.  They’re an act not to be missed. 
Check out Weird Harold’s sold-out two-night performance at the Melon Ball from December 2025!

Dec 20, 2025 
Check out Weird Harold audio tracks, live video footage, and music videos

title: Goh Kurosawa Live @ The Melon Ball
location: Watermelon Music, 1970 Lake Blvd, DAVIS, CA, 95616, United States
description:
Watermelon Music in Davis presents Goh Kurosawa Live. 
Goh Kurosawa, the “Musical Wakonyosai” or Bicultural Music Samurai, is a composer-guitarist-singer recognized for his “Lovetap” technique, percussive elements, heartfelt singing, as well as infusing fingerpicking and flamenco with electric guitar pedals. Based in California and traveling the world from Japan, his original genre blends world music, jazz, folk, rock and even classical. 

“His music takes you to that place where most people have not visited since childhood.”
“Innovative guitar creations.”
“California’s Goh Kurosawa is a multi-genre wizard who had the crowd mesmerized before his first song had ended.”
“International touring musician Goh Kurosawa’s music is beyond any simple classification. The guitarist improvises melodically, is open to the influences of pop, rock, flamenco, classical, Latin and Japanese music, and has his own musical identity. Equally skilled on electric and acoustic guitars, he uses electrical devices to create a wide range of sounds yet is not shy to embrace a pretty melody.”
“Goh’s set included Bob Marley’s No Women No Cry, My Family My Friends (original), a Japanese folk song, and Leonard Cohen’s Hallelujah (which he sang).”

title: Davis Musical Theatre Presents: RENT
location: Davis Musical Theatre Company (DMTC), The Jean Henderson Performing Arts Center, 607 Pena Drive, Davis
description:
Davis Musical Theatre Presents: RENT – June 26 through July 19, 2026
Underwritten by Nancy Dunne
Set in the East Village of New York City, Rent is about falling in love, finding your voice and living for today. Winner of the Tony Award for Best Musical and the Pulitzer Prize for Drama, Rent has become a pop cultural phenomenon. with songs that rock and a story that resonates with audiences of all ages. Based loosely on Puccini’s La Boheme, Jonathan Larson’s Rent follows a year in the life of a group of impoverished young artists and musicians struggling to survive and create in New York’s Lower East Side, under the shadow of HIV/AIDS. How these young bohemians negotiate their dreams, loves and conflicts provides the narrative thread to this groundbreaking musical. 
Recommended for theater goers 13 & up 
Directed by Kyle Jackson
Choreographed by Kyle Jackson

title: Kyle Rowland Live @ The Melon Ball
location: Watermelon Music, 1970 Lake Blvd, DAVIS, CA, 95616, United States
description:
Watermelon Music in Davis presents Kyle Rowland. 
Kyle Rowland powers through the reeds of a Harmonica, honoring the rich traditions of American rhythm & blues, soul, and gospel.  Rowland quickly and naturally developed his own sound, with help from a few of his heroes such as James Cotton, Lazy Lester, Hubert Sumlin, Billy “Boy” Arnold, Matt “Guitar” Murphy, Henry Gray, Charlie Musselwhite, and many others. Through these pioneers, Rowland learned specific techniques of stage presence, the music business, and several highly revered harmonica secrets, evident in his performances. 
In August of 2022, Rowland signed an endorsement deal with Hohner harmonica company, which he has proudly used for his 20+ year career. Recently with the help of Hohner, Rowland has had the opportunity to teach the harmonica to hundreds of children across the United States, Mexico, and Cuba. In 2024, he was inducted as the youngest member into the Sacramento Blues Hall of Fame, where he began his musical journey at the age of 10. In both 2024 and 2025, Rowland placed as a simi-finalist in the International Blues Challenge, in Memphis Tennessee.  In Spring of 2025, Rowland signed with Little Village Foundation, a California based record label, and released his critically acclaimed album NOT HOLDING BACK!, securing a 2026 Blues Music Award nomination for “Best Emerging Album.” 
Check Out Kyle’s Site for Videos and Music 
$20 General Admission
Doors open at 7:30pm
This is a BYOB event!

description:
Iama Embodied Community

title: Art in Action: Pressed Flower Suncatchers
description:
Pence Family Art Workshops
Create the perfect artwork to hang in your window! Using a circle punch, branches, pressed flowers, and other materials, craft your very own suncatcher filled with flowers and leaves.

Art in Action: Pressed Flower Suncatchers
Saturday, July 25, 1-3 PM
$5 Members, $10 Non-Members (per person, all materials included)

**How it works:**
Art in Action engages kids in art projects that are fun, creative, and collaborative with their family members. This is a drop-in program for ages 5-12. No registration in advance is required, but space and supplies are limited to the first 25 participants and are available on a first come, first served basis.

When you arrive, pay with cash or card at the front desk. A parent or adult caregiver is required to stay, but only has to pay for the project for themselves if they are also doing art. Stay as long or as short as you like over the two hour period.

Become a Member starting at $70/year and save! If you join the Pence Gallery when you attend this workshop, you can enjoy Member pricing for Art in Action, plus receive a $5 gift certificate to our gift shop as a thank you. Membership supports art for all ages and makes creative moments like this possible—jump in and be part of it.

We have a different Art in Action family workshop every month. Learn more at [https://pencegallery.org/art-in-action/](https://pencegallery.org/art-in-action/).

This monthly program is generously sponsored by Mary Stephens DeWall & Les DeWall.

title: Blood on the Clocktower at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
The first Wednesday of every month, we play _Blood on the Clocktower_, a social deduction game in the vein of Werewolf/Mafia/The Resistance, with a few twists!

We'll have a circle of chairs reserved inside Blue Note, near the back, with a Yolo County Board Game Gathering sign on the table. Just say hello, and we'll show you some games, pull some players together, and get to having fun!

We also usually have a few tables of players playing other board games, if social deduction isn't your bag!

Get a feel for Blood on the Clocktower here: https://youtu.be/4sfa8_kNxsQ
source: Meetup Yolo County Board Game Gathering

title: Relief Printmaking with Heather Hogan
description:
Pence Adult Art Programs
With artist Heather Hogan, students will learn how to design for relief printing, transfer the design to the block, use various types of ink, and create single prints and repeating patterns on paper and fabric. Paper, cards, flour-sack towels, and drawstring pouches will be provided, but students are encouraged to bring multiple garments and fabrics to print upon. Tips and techniques for collaging paper prints and securing fabric printed patches to garments will be discussed. This class is open to both beginners and experienced artists and is recommended for ages 12 and up.

Relief Printmaking with Heather Hogan
Sunday\, August 9 \| 10 AM \- 1:30 PM
$115 Members, $125 Non-Members (All materials included)

**Registration is required through the [Pence's website (CLICK HERE)](https://pencegallery.org/education/programs/workshops-and-classes/).**

Any questions? Email pencegallery@gmail.com.
